code:
$ docker run -d --name catalog -p 8080:3000 northbridge/catalog:1.4
$ docker run -d --name checkout -P northbridge/checkout:2.1
$ docker port checkout
3000/tcp -> 0.0.0.0:55001
caption: -p maps a specific, predictable port; -P publishes every EXPOSEd port to a random one each time.

eyebrow: -e for a couple of vars, --env-file for a dozen
code:
$ docker run -d --name catalog \
    --env-file catalog.env \
    northbridge/catalog:1.4

# catalog.env
NODE_ENV=production
LOG_LEVEL=info
CACHE_HOST=redis.internal
caption: One file to review and version, instead of a growing pile of -e flags.

eyebrow: docker logs -f -- the first thing to check
caption: -f follows the stream live -- what an on-call engineer runs the moment a container acts up.
